# `get_polar_axis`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Report the current polar-axis error from the saved alignment data.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build established for the cache writes) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb7c20, GetPolarFromWcs @0x15e9e0, Get3PPaError @0x160500 (64-bit build) |

Computes the angular offset between the mount axis and the celestial pole, either from the three-point error (three-point mode) or from the saved WCS images (legacy mode). Despite the name it refreshes several static caches on success.

Side effects: Rewrites the cached last-distance values on success, updates the image-centre cache and may reload the stored user location. No motion or settings write.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_polar_axis"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

| `result` | object | yes | - | (get_polar_axis success reply) Polar-axis error. The three distances are always present; success is documented as present when a cached distance exists. On failure with a valid cache, success is false, the old distances are returned and the arrays are omitted. [READ] |
| `result.dist_arcsec` | number | yes | - | (get_polar_axis success reply) Total angular distance to the pole, arcseconds (degree error times 3600). Three-point mode: from the three-point error; legacy mode: spherical separation. [READ] |
| `result.dist_x_arcsec` | number | yes | - | (get_polar_axis success reply) Azimuth-component distance, arcseconds. [READ] |
| `result.dist_y_arcsec` | number | yes | - | (get_polar_axis success reply) Altitude-component distance, arcseconds. [READ] |
| `result.success` | boolean | no | - | (get_polar_axis success reply) True when the distances were freshly computed; false when the calculation failed and the previous cached distances are returned. [READ] |
| `result.centre_deg` | array<any> | no | - | (get_polar_axis success reply) Image centre as [azimuth, altitude] degrees in horizon coordinates (not RA/Dec). Present only on the successful legacy (non-three-point) path. Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ] |
| `result.polar_deg` | array<any> | no | - | (get_polar_axis success reply) Pole position as [azimuth, altitude] degrees in horizon coordinates. Present only on the successful legacy (non-three-point) path. Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ] |

Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 207 | Legacy centre computation fails, or no usable cached distance exists | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

A failure of only the pole calculation can instead return success false with cached distances.

## Example

Request, query:

```json
{"id":101,"method":"get_polar_axis"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_polar_axis","result":{"dist_arcsec":920.5,"dist_x_arcsec":640.25,"dist_y_arcsec":660.0,"success":true,"centre_deg":[182,41],"polar_deg":[180,40]},"code":0,"id":101}
```

Reply, no-data:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_polar_axis","error":"fail to operate","code":207,"id":102}
```
